label: H-03
resolution: Folded into C-01 (acknowledged by-design). Owner already holds totalWithdrawal + emergencyWithdraw escape hatches; 24h timelock is cosmetic by design in an owner-trusted model.
severityAuditNote: Auditor: C4 convention places 'owner bypasses own timelock via sibling privileged function' at Medium/centralization, not High. Documented NatSpec is relevant but owner holds unconstrained systemic privileges.
title: withdrawAsOwner completely bypasses the totalWithdrawal 24-hour timelock, making the anti-rugpull mechanism cosmetically ineffective — owner can atomically drain all client principal in a single block
description: withdrawAsOwner routes through _withdrawInternal with no timelock, no whenNotPaused check, and no pre-announcement requirement, while totalWithdrawal in AYieldStrategy implements a 24-hour two-phase waiting period explicitly to provide community protection against rugpulls. Both functions are accessible by the same onlyOwner key. The timelock mechanism is therefore circumventable at will.
impact: A rogue or compromised owner calls withdrawAsOwner(client, attackerEOA, type(uint256).max) once per client in the same block. All client principal is converted and sent to an arbitrary recipient address with no 24-hour notice, no pause-gate, and no event field that identifies the debited client. The WithdrawalExecuted event that communities monitor to detect rugpulls is never emitted because the two-phase path is not taken.
attackPath: 1. Owner (compromised or rogue) calls withdrawAsOwner(client, attackerEOA, type(uint256).max) for each client
2. withdrawAsOwner routes through _withdrawInternal with no whenNotPaused check and no Phase-1/Phase-2 announcement
3. All client principal is swapped and transferred to attackerEOA atomically
4. The WithdrawalExecuted event — the signal community monitors for rugpull detection — is never emitted because the two-phase path is not taken
5. The only emitted event (Withdrawn) omits the client field (DEDUP-015), making on-chain forensics harder
